question.problem:
Compute the gradient of the function $f: \mathbb{R}^2 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/9e4b8dccd90c15d35317eb418a99dde9c43f12b8b2780e35292ecc291c10e92d.svg)
with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ at  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/37e7e5c54e3e7990b627649376f8f55a27db8a82b42b2375f99941793c92ff26.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Defining the matrix $A$ as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/7135a764f77153e7753bd3ab87305f8347207f12d87533565c0018588e00a00f.svg)
we have $f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{x}^T A \mathbf{x}.$

Since $A$ is not symmetric, we use the more general formula for the gradient of a quadratic function:

$$
\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} f(\mathbf{x}) = (A^T + A)\mathbf{x}
$$

First, we compute
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/e5e95b87bd905379b447b17e1ba8946579b85b6ab29831912c154591d5d7bde4.svg)
which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}+A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, compute the gradient at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/5b3d05513f25be9f2d0cc61ba21dbf3b34916f6c2fce1babc8fb4de1627171da.svg)

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}f(x) & =({A}^{T}+A)x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2+0 \\ 0-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
